A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PLeaS by the same authors. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-C are readable and support matching content across the revised layout and numbering.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original model-merging experiments, including classification accuracies, ablations and comparisons across memory budgets.

after.justification: Original ResNet experiments remain, alongside new ViT results, baseline comparisons and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The partial-permutation matching, permuted least-squares objective and layer-budget allocation method remain. Both activation and weight matching already existed in v1; v2 makes activation matching the default PLeaS variant and calls the other PLeaS-Weight. The ViT experiments do not introduce a documented new merging component.

E1.justification: V2 adds CIFAR-100 partitioned into two 50-class tasks, including joint classification, and removes the CIFAR-10/CINIC-Im experiment from v1 Appendix B.2. The central DomainNet, four fine-grained classification datasets and ImageNet coverage remain.

E2.justification: MuDSC joins the main comparison in Table 1 and replaces ZipIt! in the same-initialization comparison in Table 2. Figure 5 also introduces a constant layer-merging-ratio comparator. Most existing comparison methods remain; TaskVectors and Simple Avg represent the same baseline.

E3.justification: V2 introduces ViT evaluation protocols with CLIP-style training and classification, including joint-100-class versus within-50-class evaluation, and adds ResNet-101 configurations. The reported default PLeaS configuration switches from weight to activation matching. These are substantive experimental-setting changes, although most existing ResNet training and evaluation procedures remain.

E4.justification: New Figure 5 tests the layer-budget allocation strategy against a constant-ratio alternative. Figure 7 extends activation-versus-weight matching analysis across ResNet scales, and Figure 8 extends synthetic-data tests beyond ImageNet merging. The CIFAR/CINIC random-permutation analysis is removed; the earlier ResNet-18 benchmark is incorporated into the main figures.

E5.justification: The existing three random restarts and two model assignments, yielding six-run means and standard deviations, remain unchanged. V2 Appendix A newly reports repeating the CIFAR-50+50 partition-and-training procedure three times and averaging its results; this does not establish additional runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: V2 adds ViT, MuDSC, ResNet-101 and new ablation results, while removing the CIFAR/CINIC results. Existing entries also change: Table 1 reports PLeaS CUB/NABirds accuracies of 75.2/69.7 instead of 77.3/61.8, and Table 7 changes its 1.8x Dogs accuracy from 73.5 to 75.5. The changed default matching variant prevents interpreting headline updates as same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: The matching objectives, least-squares formulation and constrained layer-allocation approximation are retained, including the material moved from Appendix A.2 to A.3. New Appendix A.2 explains existing matching algorithms without adding a new theorem, proof or mathematical formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand demonstrated applicability from ResNets to ResNets and ViTs, while narrowing the improvement claim from 8-15 percentage points to up to 15. The central contributions concerning partial merging, least squares and merging without training-domain data remain.

C2.justification: V2 removes the convolution-only limitation and transformer future-work statement. It adds interpretations concerning matching performance across model scales and weight matching's reduced dependence on calibration data. The same-architecture restriction and additional merging-time limitation remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a PLeaS code-release link, ViT/OpenCLIP setup details, an explicit permutation-computation explanation naming the SciPy assignment solver, and a worked explanation of result aggregation. Existing ResNet hyperparameters, hardware and runtime disclosures are largely retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds MuDSC and OpenCLIP references, discusses MuDSC's relationship to PLeaS, and removes the CINIC-10 reference with its experiment. The broader related-work organization remains, with limited revisions to the positioning against ZipIt!.

P1.justification: V2 edits the abstract and surrounding prose, reorganizes Section 5 around experimental setup, fixed-size comparisons and size-accuracy tradeoffs, and revises appendix headings and variant terminology. The overall section sequence and much of the methodological exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout, with extensive float resizing and relocation. Figure 3 becomes a six-panel comparison incorporating the earlier ResNet-18 plots; new ablation figures and a ViT table appear, the CIFAR/CINIC table disappears, and Table 1 gains average columns.

improvement.justification: The MuDSC comparisons, direct layer-allocation ablation, ViT evaluation and added implementation information strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. These benefits outweigh the removed CIFAR/CINIC study, but reporting problems limit the improvement: v2 Table 2 lists MuDSC at 55.8 on Infograph versus PLeaS at 29.5, conflicting with the accompanying description of similar performance with PLeaS slightly better.
